source: ACGME Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery Milestones 2.0

level_1: Identifies potential airway emergencies as part of an evaluation team
Initiates the airway management algorithm from least to most invasive
level_2: Escalates care of emergency airway (e.g., alerts airway team)
Performs straightforward airway emergency procedures
level_3: Performs airway assessment and focused history and physical
Implements airway management plan
level_4: Describes the airway management algorithm from least to most invasive
Performs complex airway emergency procedures
level_5: Assists in straightforward airway emergency procedures
Develops anticipatory airway management plan

level_1: Performs a history and physical examination in patients with a facial trauma
Initiates work-up of common complications
Performs routine surgical management for facial trauma, assists with complex facial trauma
level_2: Assists with routine peri- operative care for facial trauma patients
Explains the risks and benefits of treatment plans for facial trauma
Manages uncommon/infrequent complications
level_3: Recognizes common complications
Assists with routine surgical management for facial trauma
Adapts standard treatment plans and techniques to special circumstances
level_4: Formulates a diagnostic and treatment plan for a patient with facial trauma
Manages common complications and recognizes uncommon/infrequent complications
Performs operative management of complex facial trauma
level_5: Provides routine peri- operative care for facial trauma patients
Describes typical treatment plan
Serves as a peer resource for managing uncommon/infrequent complications

level_1: Performs a history and physical examination in patients with head and neck neoplasm
Initiates work-up of common complications
Performs routine surgical management for head and neck disease, assists with complex head and neck neoplasm
level_2: Assists with routine peri- operative care for patients with head and neck neoplasm
Explains the risks and benefits of treatment plans for head and neck neoplasm
Manages uncommon/infrequent complications
level_3: Recognizes common complications
Assists with routine surgical management for head and neck neoplasm
Adapts standard treatment plans and techniques to special circumstances
level_4: Formulates a diagnostic plan for a patient with head and neck neoplasm
Manages common complications and recognizes uncommon/infrequent complications
Performs operative management of complex head and neck neoplasm
level_5: Provides routine peri- operative care for patients with head and neck neoplasm
Describes typical treatment plan
Serves as a peer resource for managing uncommon/infrequent complications

level_1: Performs a history and physical examination in patients with ear disease and/or hearing loss
Identifies surgical and disease-relevant anatomy on a computerized tomography (CT) scan
Dissects middle ear structures, performs a facial recess approach, and performs an ossicular reconstruction and cholesteatoma dissection
level_2: Assists with set-up, performs placement of ventilation tubes, and opens and closes postauricular incisions
Orders routine diagnostic studies for ear disease and/or hearing loss
Interprets specialized audiometric and vestibular testing
level_3: Interprets routine audiograms
Begins to perform middle ear dissection
Adapts standard treatment plans and interventions to special circumstances
level_4: Formulates a diagnostic and treatment plan for a patient with ear disease and/or hearing loss
Identifies normal and disease-relevant anatomy on a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
Skeletonizes facial nerve, sigmoid sinus, and dura, and begins to perform lateral temporal bone resection
level_5: Elevates tympanomeatal flap, performs cortical mastoidectomy
Explains the risks, benefits, and alternatives of medical and surgical interventions for ear disease and/or hearing loss
Leads an otology patient care conference

level_1: Performs a history and physical examination in a patient with rhinologic disease
Initiates work-up of common complications associated with rhinologic disease
Performs routine surgical management and assists with complex surgical management for patients with rhinologic disease
level_2: Assists with routine perioperative care for patients with rhinologic disease
Explains the risks and benefits of treatment plans for rhinologic disease
Manages uncommon/infrequent complications associated with rhinologic disease
level_3: Recognizes common complications associated with rhinologic disease
Assists with routine surgical management for patients with rhinologic disease
Adapts standard treatment plans and techniques to special circumstances
level_4: Formulates a diagnostic and treatment plan for a patient with rhinologic disease
Manages common complications and recognizes uncommon/infrequent complications associated with rhinologic disease
Performs complex surgical management for patients with rhinologic disease
level_5: Provides routine perioperative care for patients with rhinologic disease
Identifies when typical treatment plans should be modified
Serves as a peer resource for managing uncommon/infrequent complications associated with rhinologic disease

level_1: Performs a history and physical examination in patients with laryngologic disease
Initiates work-up of common complications associated with laryngologic disease
Performs routine surgical management and assists with complex surgical management for patients with laryngologic disease
level_2: Assists with routine perioperative care for patients with laryngologic disease
Explains the risks and benefits of treatment plans for laryngologic disease
Manages uncommon/infrequent complications associated with laryngologic disease
level_3: Recognizes common complications associated with laryngologic disease
Assists with routine surgical management for patients with laryngologic disease, including direct laryngoscopy, microlaryngeal techniques, and vocal fold injections
Adapts standard treatment plans and techniques to special circumstances
level_4: Formulates a diagnostic and treatment plan for a patient with laryngologic disease
Manages common complications and recognizes uncommon/infrequent complications associated with laryngologic disease
Performs complex surgical management for patients with laryngologic disease, including laryngotracheal reconstruction and arytenoid procedures
level_5: Provides routine perioperative care for patients with laryngologic disease, including both direct and indirect laryngoscopy
Identifies when typical treatment plans should be modified
Serves as a peer resource for managing uncommon/infrequent complications associated with laryngologic disease

level_1: Performs an age- appropriate history and physical examination with developmental assessment
Recognizes and initiates work-up of routine complications of treatment
Performs airway and soft tissue pediatric procedures; assists with complex pediatric procedures
level_2: Assists with pediatric otolaryngology procedures
Explains the risks and benefits of pediatric procedures; adapts diagnoses to age-related variations
Manages uncommon complications of treatment
level_3: Provides routine peri- operative care for pediatric otolaryngology procedures
Performs routine pediatric procedures on atypical patients (e.g., syndromic), and airway and soft tissue pediatric otolaryngology procedures (e.g., bronchoscopy, branchial cleft excision)
Actively participates in discussion at an interdisciplinary pediatric case conference or specialty clinic
level_4: Formulates a diagnostic and treatment plan for a pediatric patient
Manages routine complications and recognizes complex complications of treatment
Performs complex pediatric otolaryngology procedures
level_5: Performs routine pediatric procedures on typical patients (e.g., ear tube placement, tonsillectomy, adenoidectomy)
Adapts standard treatment plans to special circumstances (e.g., syndromic children and infants)
Serves as a peer resource for managing uncommon/infrequent complications associated with pediatric procedures

level_1: Performs a history and physical examination in patients with aesthetic/functional concerns
Initiates work-up of common complications
Performs routine surgical management for patients requiring head and neck aesthetic/functional surgery
level_2: Assists with routine peri- operative care for patients receiving head and neck aesthetic/functional surgery
Explains the risks and benefits of treatment plans for aesthetic/functional surgery
Manages uncommon/infrequent complications
level_3: Recognizes common complications
Assists with routine surgical management for head and neck aesthetic/functional surgery
Adapts standard treatment plans and techniques to special circumstances
level_4: Formulates a diagnostic and treatment plan for a patient with aesthetic/functional concerns
Manages common complications and recognizes uncommon/infrequent complications
Performs operative management of complex head and neck aesthetic/functional surgery
level_5: Provides routine peri- operative care for patients receiving head and neck aesthetic/functional surgery
Identifies best treatment plan to address patient concerns
Serves as a peer resource for managing uncommon/infrequent complications

level_1: Performs a history and physical examination in a patient with sleep concerns
Initiates work-up of common complications associated with sleep surgery and sleep disorders
Performs common surgical management of sleep disorders
level_2: Assists with routine peri- operative care for sleep surgery patients
Explains the risks and benefits of treatment plans for sleep disorders
Manages uncommon/infrequent complications associated with sleep surgery and sleep disorders
level_3: Recognizes common complications of sleep surgery and sleep disorders
Assists with routine surgical management of sleep disorders
Adapts standard treatment plans for sleep disorders to individual circumstances
level_4: Formulates a diagnostic and treatment plan for a patient with sleep concerns
Manages common complications and recognizes uncommon/infrequent complications associated with sleep surgery and sleep disorders
Performs complex surgical management of sleep disorders
level_5: Provides routine peri- operative care for sleep surgery patients
Identifies when standard sleep interventions should be modified
Serves as a peer resource for managing uncommon/infrequent complications

level_1: Identifies normal anatomy during common operations
Articulates the steps of complex operations
level_2: Articulates the steps of common operations
Identifies variations in anatomy during complex operations
level_3: Identifies variations in anatomy during common operations
Articulates the implications of varying anatomy on the steps of complex operations
level_4: Articulates the implications of varying anatomy on the steps of common operations
Leads anatomy instruction for students and co- residents
level_5: Identifies normal anatomy during complex operations
Teaches complex variations of anatomy and implications for surgical approaches

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of allergic hypersensitivity and resulting clinical manifestations
Demonstrates knowledge of risk factors associated with systemic reaction to allergen exposure
Determines appropriateness of antigen-specific immunotherapy
level_2: Explains common clinical manifestations of hypersensitivity and allergic disease
Demonstrates knowledge of interventions, including avoidance, pharmacotherapy, and antigen-specific immunotherapy
Describes the basic intervention and treatment of anaphylaxis
level_3: Describes the potential severity of severe allergic responses
Articulates a treatment plan for clinical manifestations of allergic rhinitis
Reliably resolves discrepancies between testing results and clinical findings
level_4: Discusses pathophysiology of immunoglobulin E (IgE) – mediated hypersensitivity and roles of exposure and sensitization
Describes the early signs of anaphylaxis and/or systemic reaction
Synthesizes data to modify testing strategies and treatment for difficult/high-risk patients
level_5: Explains common complications and comorbid conditions associated with allergic disease
Interprets data from allergy in-vitro or skin testing
Describes advanced treatment of anaphylaxis

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of normal physiology, pathophysiology, and clinical findings for otolaryngologic conditions routinely managed by non- otolaryngologists
level_2: Demonstrates basic knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for common otolaryngologic conditions
level_3: Demonstrates advanced knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for commonly encountered otolaryngologic conditions
level_4: Demonstrates knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for uncommon otolaryngologic conditions
level_5: Contributes new knowledge for pathophysiology and clinical findings for otolaryngologic conditions (e.g., publication, curriculum development)

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes local quality improvement initiatives
Discloses patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies specific population and community health needs for their local population
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems including outpatient settings
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of their interprofessional teams
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
Leads innovations and advocates for populations and communities with specific health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
Describes core administrative knowledge needed for transition to practice (e.g., contract negotiations, malpractice insurance, government regulation, compliance)
Advocates for patient care needs (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources) with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems, including government, private, public, uninsured care, and practice models
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Analyzes individual practice patterns and professional requirements in preparation for practice
level_3: Identifies basic knowledge domains for effective transition to practice (e.g., information technology, legal, billing and coding, financial, personnel)
Engages with patients in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment models
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care and transition of care
level_4: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Demonstrates use of information technology required for medical practice (e.g., electronic health record, documentation required for billing and coding)
Participates in health policy advocacy activities
level_5: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model (e.g., insurance type)
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transition of care
Educates others to prepare them for transition to practice

level_1: Demonstrates how to access available evidence, and incorporate patient preferences and values to take care of a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide care to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients; and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Designs and implements a learning plan, with prompting
Challenges assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the factors which contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data episodically, with adaptability
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and when necessary, improves it
level_3: Actively seeks opportunities to improve
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Role models consistently seeking performance data with adaptability
level_4: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Coaches others on reflective practice
level_5: Analyzes and reflects on the factors which contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Intentionally seeks performance data consistently with adaptability
Facilitates the design and implementing learning plans for others

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles and recognizes need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying patient care, including informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, and related topics
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in self and others
level_3: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations and how to appropriately report professionalism lapses
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed
level_4: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
Leads system outcomes
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

subcompetencies.name: Knowledge of Systemic and Individual Factors of Well-Being

level_1: Recognizes the importance of getting help when needed to address personal and professional well-being
Reflects on actions in real time to proactively respond to the inherent emotional challenges of physician work
level_2: Lists resources to support personal and professional well-being
Suggests potential solutions to institutional factors that affect well- being
level_3: Recognizes that institutional factors affect well-being
Participates in institutional changes to promote personal and professional well-being
level_4: With prompting, reflects on how personal and professional well-being may impact one’s clinical practice
level_5: Describes institutional factors that affect well- being

level_1: Uses language and nonverbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport
Organizes and initiates communication with patient/family by introducing stakeholders, setting the agenda, clarifying expectations, and verifying understanding of the clinical situation
Independently recognizes biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication (e.g., language, disability) while accurately communicating own role within the health care system
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters
Independently, uses shared decision making to align patient/family values, goals, and preferences with treatment options to make a personalized care plan
level_3: Identifies the need to adjust communication strategies based on assessment of patient/family expectations and understanding of their health status and treatment options
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and clear language
With guidance, sensitively and compassionately delivers medical information, elicits patient/family values, goals, and preferences, and acknowledges uncertainty and conflict
Role models self- awareness while identifying a contextual approach to minimize communication barriers
level_5: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy)
Easily establishes therapeutic relationships, with attention to patient/family concerns and context, regardless of complexity
Role models shared decision making in patient/family communication including those with a high degree of uncertainty/conflict

level_1: Respectfully requests/receives a consultation
Receives follow-up and feedback on the outcome of the consultation
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
level_2: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Uses active listening to adapt communication style to fit team needs
Role models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_3: Clearly and concisely requests/responds to a consultation
Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Facilitates health care team-based feedback in complex situations
level_4: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care
Facilitates teaching of team-based communication and feedback
level_5: Respectfully receives feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Communicates feedback and constructive criticism to superiors

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record
Appropriately selects direct (e.g., telephone, in- person) and indirect (e.g., progress notes, text messages) forms of communication based on context
level_2: Safeguards patient personal health information
Communicates clearly, concisely, timely, and in an organized written form, including anticipatory guidance
level_3: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record
Achieves written or verbal communication (e.g., patient notes, email) that serves as an example for others to follow
level_4: Documents required data in formats specified by institutional policy
Models feedback to improve others’ written communication
level_5: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
Guides departmental or institutional communication around policies and procedures
